The Coastal Adaptation Facility announced in 2026 that climate finance would support 42 local projects in developing countries. The programme links renewable energy, flood-resilient schools, and technology transfer for small municipalities. It reports that solar and wind training reduced diesel dependence by 18 percent in pilot districts.

The facility works with the United Nations Development Programme and local energy agencies. Its public briefing says that transparent reporting, community consultation, and maintenance training are required before grants are released. The speech evidence should focus on practical adaptation, not abstract climate slogans.
